extracted.intended_audience: radio, television, and digital news organizations and entrants preparing submissions for the Edward R. Murrow Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Rules and category-specific submission criteria for Edward R. Murrow Awards (radio, television, and digital divisions), including division definitions, partnership/market rules, category time limits, editing/voice-over policies, URL/run-time limits, and documentation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proper division and region submission / reclassification
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries must be submitted in the proper division and region to be considered for judging. Entrants that do not enter correctly will be disqualified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Market size is determined by MSA ranking for radio entries and by DMA ranking for television entries. RTDNA reserves the sole right to reclassify the submission without prior notice to the entrant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Large Market Station (Radio & Television)
rubrics_metrics.description: Large Market Station: Markets 1 - 50.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the MSA (radio) or DMA (television) ranking to determine market placement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small Market Station (Radio & Television)
rubrics_metrics.description: Small Market Station: Markets 51+.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stations in markets ranked 51 and above enter as small market.

rubrics_metrics.name: Network / Syndication / Program Service classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Network, Syndication Service, Program Service: Any organization that programs to multiple markets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applies to organizations whose programming reaches multiple markets rather than a single-market station.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital News Organization definition
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital News Organizations: 'Pure Play' digital organizations; no portion of digital entries should have been broadcast.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrant must be primarily an online news organization and not have broadcast-origin content in the submitted material.

rubrics_metrics.name: Small vs Large Digital thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: Small Digital News Organization: 2,499,999 or fewer unique visitors per month. Large Digital News Organizations: 2,500,000 or more unique visitors per month.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entrants are categorized by monthly unique visitors; documentation/verification is required (see Verification of Digital Size).

rubrics_metrics.name: Verification of Digital Size
rubrics_metrics.description: Digital News Organization entrants are required to send verification of Monthly Unique Visitors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no verification is sent, RTDNA reserves the sole right to reclassify the submission without prior notice to the entrant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital entries judged at national level
rubrics_metrics.description: Both Small and Large Digital entries will be judged only at the national level.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Digital divisions are not judged by local/regional rounds — national-only judging applies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partnership submission rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Any entry produced in a partnership must be submitted in the market and region of the largest partner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A 'partner' is defined as someone who provides production assistance or significant editorial input. If an organization only helps distribute work, they are not considered a partner. All partner organizations must be listed on the award entry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual licensee submission rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Enter video content into TV categories, audio content into Radio categories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Organizations with dual licenses must submit material in the matching medium category (audio→Radio, video→TV).

rubrics_metrics.name: State-wide networks & regional collaborations rule
rubrics_metrics.description: State-wide networks should submit in the largest market size in their state. Regional collaborations should submit in the market size and region of the largest partner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use the largest partner's market/region for classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Terrestrial, satellite & digital radio classification
rubrics_metrics.description: A terrestrial station also broadcast via satellite and/or online counts as a radio station in the appropriate market size. A purely satellite station should apply in the 'Network' radio category. A purely digital radio station without a terrestrial station should enter in the digital category.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Classification depends on origin/platform, not distribution channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in Diversity, Equity & Inclusion (TV & Radio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Honors outstanding journalism tackling the topic of diversity, racial injustice and/or inequality. The storytelling must bring an awareness to an issue(s) and potentially bring about a solution or dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The piece can be digital, video, audio, or all three; can be a single piece or a series; 30-minute time limit; entry may be edited and all commercial breaks must be removed; voice-overs or narratives are permitted only if they were part of the original piece; a short description of the entry is requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Podcast (TV & Radio division acceptance of podcast entries)
rubrics_metrics.description: Podcasts are defined as digital audio files made available on the internet for downloading ... typically available as a series. Entry must demonstrate original and outstanding journalistic enterprise on an important issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry may feature a single episode or an edited overview of a series; entry may be edited and all commercial breaks must be removed; voice-overs/narratives permitted only if part of the original piece; a short description is requested; entry must not exceed 30 minutes; entrants should provide an active link to the full podcast series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Newscast
rubrics_metrics.description: Only regularly scheduled newscasts are eligible for entry, and only one entry is allowed per station. Networks can submit one entry per news program.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commercial breaks must be removed but no other editing is allowed; voice-overs or narratives are permitted only if they were part of the original piece; entry must not exceed 30 minutes — if longer, submit only the first 30 minutes; a short description is requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Breaking News Coverage (first 24 hours)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry should only contain coverage from first 24 hours after the news event. Submit coverage of a single, unscheduled news event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry may be edited and all commercial breaks must be removed; voice-overs/narratives permitted only if part of the original piece; entry must not exceed 20 minutes; a short description is requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigative Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry must demonstrate original and outstanding journalistic enterprise on an important issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry may include undercover materials, demonstrate extensive research of documents and records, and include records/documentation of allegations; entry may be edited and all commercial breaks must be removed; voice-overs/narratives permitted only if part of the original piece; a short description is requested; entry must not exceed 15 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hard News
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a single hard news report prepared for a scheduled newscast that is not breaking news and not primarily investigative in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humorous or soft-topic stories do not belong here; report must have appeared on a regularly scheduled news program; entry may not be entered in Feature Reporting; entry may be edited; voice-overs/narratives permitted only if part of the original piece; a short description is requested; entry must not exceed 10 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing Coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit an entry showing continuing coverage of a major developing story over an extended period of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry may be edited (commercial breaks removed); voice-overs/narratives permitted only if part of the original piece; entry should include at least one complete news report; entry must not exceed 30 minutes; a short description is requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Series
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit coverage of a single subject reported in multiple parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry may be edited; voice-overs/narratives permitted only if part of the original piece; a short description is requested; entry must not exceed 30 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature Reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a single report covering a human-interest or profile subject that is not breaking news or investigative in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Report must have appeared on a regularly scheduled news program; entry may not be entered in Hard News; entry may be edited; voice-overs/narratives permitted only if part of the original piece; a short description is requested; entry must not exceed 10 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sports Reporting (TV & Radio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a single packaged report reflecting a journalistic endeavor to report on a newsworthy sports-related subject. Anchored sports segments within programs, stand-alone sports programs and play-by-play are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry must be unedited; a short description is requested; entry must not exceed 10 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in Sound (Radio & Digital entrants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit coverage of a single subject reported in a single segment showing creative use of sound to tell a story. This category is open to both radio and digital news organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry must be exactly as it was heard on the air or online; 'Year-ender' packages are not allowed; entry must not exceed 10 minutes; a short description is requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in Video (Television & Digital entrants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit coverage of a single subject reported in a single segment showing creative use of video to tell a story. This category is open to both television and digital news organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry must be exactly as it appeared on air or online; 'Year-ender' packages are not allowed; entry must not exceed 10 minutes; a short description is requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: News Documentary (TV & Radio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit coverage of a single subject reported in a single segment addressing a need or needs of your market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry may be edited; voice-overs/narratives permitted only if they were part of the original piece; entry must not exceed 60 minutes; a short description is requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Feature-Length Documentary (Network Television only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit coverage of a single subject reported in a single segment addressing a need or needs of your audience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry may be edited; voice-overs/narratives permitted only if they were part of the original piece; entry must be more than 60 minutes in length; a short description is requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in Writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit an entry that demonstrates excellence in writing that conveys the feeling and significance of events to the listener or viewer.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry may represent individual or collaborative effort and may include up to three examples, exactly as it originally appeared; a script of each example must accompany the entry; a short description is requested; entry must not exceed 15 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Excellence in Innovation (legacy radio/TV organizations)
rubrics_metrics.description: Designed to award legacy radio or television news organizations that innovate their product to enhance the quality of journalism and the audience’s understanding of news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a single entry that demonstrates an innovative use of content, engagement, technology and/or audience experience. A single entry may include audio or video examples; functioning, cached or active URLs; apps; social feeds; or any other platform that demonstrates innovation in journalism. Audio or video entries must not exceed 30 minutes (if longer, submit first 30 minutes). Commercial breaks must be removed but no other editing is allowed. A written description explaining how the entry breaks the mold of traditional broadcast journalism is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital (Television & Radio Entrants Only)
rubrics_metrics.description: Category expanded to allow stations to showcase their website and/or multimedia (broadcast, digital and social media) approach to stories. Entries can either be an overview of web presence or focus on multimedia coverage of a single news topic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The news organization's online presence must disseminate timely news and information targeted for core audiences; news content must be generated primarily by entrant. Submit UP TO 5 examples of functioning, cached or active URLs that demonstrate exceptional news coverage and journalistic skill (this is a change). If entry includes audio/video content, total run time may not exceed 30 minutes. Entry must include original content. Creativity, clarity, storytelling techniques, and use of audio, video or other Internet technologies will be considered by the judges. A short description is requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Excellence (TV & Radio)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a single entry that contains examples of breaking news, continuing coverage, features and/or other work, including your web presence that reflects the depth and scope of the news organization.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be eligible, TV and Radio Stations must enter at least two other categories including: Breaking News, Hard News, Investigative Reporting, Continuing Coverage, or Newscast. Entrants are no longer required to submit their newscast with the overall excellence entry. Entry must include examples of a robust Web and digital media presence; entrants are limited to 5 links for digital examples in addition to the 40 minutes of audio/video content for the entry. Entry may be edited (commercial breaks removed); voice-overs/narratives permitted only if part of original; judging based on original work samples not on the way the entry is produced; entry must not exceed 40 minutes; a written rundown is required for audio and video.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Division: News Series (URL-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit up to five functioning, cached or active URLs linking to coverage of a single subject reported in multiple parts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A short description is requested. If entry includes audio/video content, total run time may not exceed 30 minutes. Entry may be edited.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Division: Excellence in Diversity, Equity & Inclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: Honors outstanding journalism tackling diversity, racial injustice and/or inequality. The storytelling must bring an awareness to an issue(s) and potentially bring about a solution or dialogue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Piece can be digital, video, audio, or all three; can be single piece or a series around a single topic; 30-minute time limit; a short description is requested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Division: Podcast (URL-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Podcasts are defined as digital audio files ... Entry must demonstrate original and outstanding journalistic enterprise on an important issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry may feature a single episode or an edited overview of a series; may be edited and commercial breaks removed; voice-overs/narratives permitted only if part of the original piece; a short description is requested; entry must not exceed 30 minutes; entrants should provide an active link to the full podcast series.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Division: Breaking News Coverage (URL-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Entry should only contain coverage from first 24 hours after the news event. Submit coverage of a single, unscheduled news event.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit up to five functioning, cached or active URLs linking to coverage of the single, unscheduled news event; a short description is requested; if includes audio/video content, total run time may not exceed 20 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Division: Investigative Reporting (URL-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit up to five functioning, cached or active URLs linking to an entry which must demonstrate original and outstanding journalistic enterprise on an important issue.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry may include materials from undercover sources, demonstrate extensive research of documents and records, and include records and documentation of allegations; a short description is requested; if includes audio/video content, total run time may not exceed 15 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Division: Hard News (URL-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a functioning, cached or active URL linking to an entry which consists of a single hard news report that is not breaking news and not primarily investigative in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humorous or soft-topic stories do not belong here; entry may not be entered in Feature Reporting; a short description is requested; if includes audio/video content, total run time may not exceed 10 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Division: Continuing Coverage (URL-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit an entry showing continuing coverage of a major developing story over an extended period of time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit up to five functioning, cached or active URLs linking to coverage; entry should include at least one complete news report; a short description is requested; if includes audio/video content, total run time may not exceed 30 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Division: Feature Reporting (URL-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a functioning, cached or active URL linking to a single report covering a human-interest or profile subject that is not breaking news or investigative in nature.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry may not be entered in Hard News; a short description is requested; if includes audio/video content, total run time may not exceed 10 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Division: Sports Reporting (URL-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a single packaged report reflecting a journalistic endeavor to report on a newsworthy sports-related subject. Anchored sports segments within programs, stand-alone sports programs and play-by-play are not eligible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry must be unedited; a short description is requested; entry must not exceed 10 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Division: Excellence in Sound (URL-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a functioning, cached or active URL linking to a single subject reported in a single segment showing creative use of sound to tell a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry must be exactly as it was heard on a digital platform or platforms; 'Year-ender' packages are not allowed; a short description is requested; total run time may not exceed 10 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Division: Excellence in Video (URL-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a functioning, cached or active URL linking to a single subject reported in a single segment showing creative use of video to tell a story.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry must be exactly as it appeared on a digital platform or platforms; 'Year-ender' packages are not allowed; a short description is requested; total run time may not exceed 10 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Division: News Documentary (URL-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a functioning, cached or active URL linking to a single subject reported in a single segment addressing a need or needs of your users.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry may be edited; a short description is requested; if entry includes audio/video content, total run time may not exceed 60 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Division: Excellence in Writing (URL-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit a functioning, cached or active URL to an entry demonstrating excellence in writing that conveys the feeling and significance of events to the user.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entry may represent individual or collaborative effort and may include up to three examples, exactly as it originally appeared; a short description is requested; if entry includes audio/video content, total run time may not exceed 15 minutes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Division: Excellence in Innovation (URL-based)
rubrics_metrics.description: Designed to award digital news organizations that innovate their product to enhance the quality of journalism and the audience’s understanding of news.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submit a functioning, cached or active URL linking to a single entry that demonstrates an innovative use of content, engagement, technology and/or audience experience. A single entry may include audio/video examples, functioning URLs, apps, social feeds, or any platform that demonstrates innovation. Audio or video entries must not exceed 30 minutes (if longer, submit only first 30). No editing is allowed. A written description explaining how the entry breaks the mold of traditional journalism is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Digital Division: Overall Excellence
rubrics_metrics.description: Submit an entry that contains up to ten live or cached URLs linking to examples of breaking news, continuing coverage, features and/or other work that reflects the depth and scope of the news organization. Apps and social feeds may also be submitted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: To be eligible, Digital News Organizations must enter at least two other categories. If entry includes audio/video content, total run time may not exceed 40 minutes. Judging will be based on original work samples not on the way the entry is produced.
